job_heading: The Job: What We Found, What We Did
job_lead: The homeowner kept the fireplace and changed what burns in it. The detail photo is the burner on test.

found.text: An existing fireplace in good condition, with a sound firebox, and a homeowner who wanted the convenience of gas: heat at the push of a button, no wood to store, no ash to clean out. The job was to set a new gas burner system into the firebox the house already had, rather than replace the fireplace.

A gas install starts the same way every Northmark job does — with the chimney and firebox, not the appliance. A fireplace that will burn gas still vents through the flue, so the flue has to be clear and the firebox sound before anything is connected.

steps.title: Firebox and flue checked
steps.text: The firebox, damper and flue were inspected and photographed before the install, so the new system vents into a chimney that is actually ready for it.

steps.title: Firebox prepared
steps.text: The firebox was cleared and prepared, and the burner position set so the flames sit where the log set and the venting expect them.

steps.title: Burner system set
steps.text: The burner assembly, grate and electronic ignition module were set and secured in the firebox, with the ignition wiring routed clear of the heat.

steps.title: Gas connected and commissioned
steps.text: In Ontario, the gas connection is regulated work: it is made by a TSSA-certified gas technician, with the connection checked for leaks before the appliance is lit.

steps.title: Test burn and hand-over
steps.text: The system was run through a full test burn — the photo at the top of the page — and the homeowner was walked through lighting, shutting off and what to watch for.

why_heading: Gas In An Existing Fireplace: What To Know
why_lead: The fireplace you have is usually the right place for gas. Three things decide whether it is a good fit.

pillars.title: The fireplace stays
pillars.text: A gas burner or log set goes into the firebox you already have. The mantel, the surround and the room stay as they are — what changes is the fuel.

pillars.title: Venting and safety first
pillars.text: Gas still produces combustion gases. The flue, damper and firebox are checked before anything is connected, and the gas connection is made by a certified technician.

pillars.title: The chimney still needs looking after
pillars.text: A gas fireplace vents through the same chimney. A yearly inspection keeps the flue clear and catches moisture damage early — gas exhaust is wet.

faq.q: Can you put a gas burner into my wood-burning fireplace?
faq.a: Often, yes. It depends on the condition of the firebox and flue and on getting a gas line to the fireplace. Tell us what you have when you book; the free inspection confirms whether your fireplace is a fit and what the job involves.

In Ontario, gas appliance connections are regulated by the TSSA and must be made by a certified gas technician. We confirm how your job is handled, and who does what, when you book — before anything is scheduled.

faq.q: Does a gas fireplace still need a chimney inspection?
faq.a: Yes. A gas fireplace in a masonry fireplace vents through the chimney, and gas exhaust carries a lot of moisture, which works on the flue over time. A yearly inspection keeps the flue clear and catches damage early.

faq.q: My gas fireplace will not light or stay lit. Is that something you fix?
faq.a: Yes — tell us the make if you know it and what it is doing or not doing, and we confirm it is a fit before anything is booked. See fireplace repair.

faq.q: Do you install gas fireplaces across the GTA?
faq.a: Toronto and the GTA — Etobicoke to Scarborough, and north through Vaughan, Richmond Hill and Markham. See where we work.
